desc: Pure vision framework using fine-tuned YOLO for Set-of-Marks prompting to localize UI elements without brittle accessibility trees.
examplePrompt: Automate adding a calendar event in Outlook desktop: open new event, fill title 'Sprint review', set time tomorrow 10am, invite team@. Use SoMatic marks to locate fields and buttons reliably.
features: YOLO-based detection of text and interactables with ONNX CPU inference
Set-of-Marks overlay with stable numeric IDs
No dependency on accessibility tree or DOM
Mapping from mark ID to center coordinates for click/type
Designed for native OS RPA and agent grounding
longDesc: SoMatic applies Set-of-Marks methodology to native OS automation. A local YOLO model detects text and interactive elements, draws labeled bounding boxes, and maps IDs to coordinates, letting LLMs reference elements by ID instead of pixel coordinates. This enables reliable computer-use agents on desktop apps where accessibility trees are missing or non-deterministic. Runs on CPU with ONNX and is inspired by OmniParser v2.
name: SoMatic: Vision-Grounded UI Automation
prompt: You are a Computer-Use Grounding Engineer. Capture screen, run SoMatic to generate Set-of-Marks overlay, reason about task using mark IDs, and output actions as click/type on IDs. Verify grounding before execution.

desc: Structured framework where agents write verbal self-reflections after trials and store them in episodic memory to improve future attempts.
examplePrompt: Solve this Python coding challenge with Reflexion: implement rate limiter with token bucket. Run tests, reflect on failures, and improve solution across 3 iterations.
features: Verbal reinforcement via natural language memory
Works with frozen LLMs, no fine-tuning needed
Proven gains on HumanEval, AlfWorld, HotPotQA
longDesc: Reflexion augments agents with a critic that generates natural language reflections on failures or successes, which are saved to memory and retrieved in subsequent episodes. It implements a try-reflect-retry loop with separate Actor, Evaluator, and Self-Reflection modules. This yields state-of-the-art gains on coding, reasoning, and decision-making benchmarks without model fine-tuning.
name: Reflexion: Self-Critique Agent Loop
prompt: You are a Reflexion Coach. Run the agent on the task, evaluate outcome, generate a concise self-reflection identifying the specific failure mode and fix, store it, then retry with reflection in context. Iterate until success or budget exhausted.

desc: Reasoning framework that models thoughts as nodes in a graph with arbitrary topology, enabling aggregation, refinement, and branching beyond chains or trees.
examplePrompt: Use Graph-of-Thoughts to sort 32 numbers with minimal comparisons: generate partial sorts, aggregate merges, refine ordering, and output sorted list with operation trace.
features: Controller for adaptive expansion and scoring
Outperforms CoT and ToT on sorting and set tasks
Modular operations for custom reasoning schemes
longDesc: Graph-of-Thoughts generalizes Chain-of-Thought and Tree-of-Thoughts by representing the reasoning process as a directed graph. Thoughts can be generated, aggregated, refined, and scored; the controller decides expansion operations. This allows merging partial solutions, backtracking, and exploring combinatorial spaces efficiently for sorting, set operations, and creative writing tasks.
name: Graph-of-Thoughts: Structured Reasoning
prompt: You are a Graph-of-Thoughts Orchestrator. Decompose problem into thought nodes, expand graph with generate and aggregate operations, score nodes, and synthesize final answer from best path.
